items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: You know I think he did it that way because he saw Joe Mooney do it that way... And that’s when we learned tunes he would just start to play it and I’d go like that.

ctx.x: Yeah you said it was the hardest thing and the most valuable thing, or something like that.

You know I think he did it that way because he saw Joe Mooney do it that way. Joe Mooney was the blind accordion player from Paterson and he would go watch their rehearsals, the quartet, on Sundays at Sandy’s Hollywood in Paterson. And I think Joe, he © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

would go, “Here’s what you’re going to play” [scats] and he’d go to the guitar player, “here’s what you’re going to play” and you had to hear it and play it. It wasn’t like Joe was writing out charts for the band. This was here now let’s all try it together. And that’s when we learned tunes he would just start to play it and I’d go like that.
